edges.description: Loss of the extracellular PPi anti-mineralization brake permits hydroxyapatite deposition; mineralized arterial walls and secondary remodeling produce the defining calcification and stenosis.
intermediate_mechanisms: Hydroxyapatite deposition in the arterial internal elastic lamina

edges.description: Deficient AMP/adenosine signaling is proposed to promote myointimal proliferation, narrowing muscular arteries alongside the mineralization branch.
Ectopic mineralization in arterial walls manifests as vascular calcification.
Arterial mineralization and intimal proliferation narrow affected vessels.
Diffuse arterial narrowing and stiffness increase vascular resistance.
intermediate_mechanisms: Increased arterial stiffness and vascular resistance

edges.description: Severe diffuse arterial disease increases cardiac workload and can cause heart failure.
intermediate_mechanisms: Increased ventricular afterload and myocardial ischemia

edges.description: FGF23-associated renal phosphate depletion impairs skeletal mineralization and produces hypophosphatemic rickets.
intermediate_mechanisms: Renal phosphate wasting and chronic hypophosphatemia

edges.description: Hearing loss is a frequent ENPP1-survivor association, but its directness and intermediates are not established.

edges.description: Low plasma PPi reports the proximal loss of the extracellular anti-mineralization brake, although assay availability and diagnostic thresholds are not established here.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and Molecular Characterization of a Patient with Generalized Arterial Calcification of Infancy Caused by Rare ABCC6 Mutation.
evidence.snippet: We have identified the underlying cause as biallelic mutations in ABCC6 (NM_00117: exon30, c.4223_4227dupAGCTC p.(Leu1410Serfs*56)) and a unique exonic deletion that spans from the first to the fourth exons of ABCC6 (chr16:16313388-16330869)).
